_about: Approved by Nav on 2026-11-19 (phase 7a; Olympus Mons reworded 2026-11-20). The Earth → Mars leg's detours for the daily vote (moved here from content/vote-options.json in E3). One detour a day, avoiding the last 3 days' picks. hours: how much later the arrival (applied at today's pace). Every fact checked against its source.

detours.label: Detour for a photo of Earth and the Moon together: about 4 hours later
detours.fact: The Moon is a little over a quarter of Earth's width: about 3,475 km across, against Earth's 12,742 km.

detours.label: Turn the camera on Venus: about 2 hours later
detours.fact: Venus is the hottest planet in the Solar System, hotter even than Mercury: its surface is about 465 °C.

detours.label: Swing by a passing asteroid for a close-up: about 3 hours later
detours.fact: Most known asteroids orbit the Sun in the main belt, between Mars and Jupiter.

detours.label: Photograph Jupiter from afar: about 1 hour later
detours.fact: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets put together.

detours.label: Stop to measure the solar wind: about 1 hour later
detours.fact: The solar wind streams out from the Sun at around 400 km a second, about 20 times faster than our probe coasts.

detours.label: Point the telescope at the moons of Mars: about 2 hours later
detours.fact: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos. Phobos, the bigger one, is only about 22 km across.

detours.label: Zoom in on Olympus Mons: about 2 hours later
detours.fact: Olympus Mons on Mars is the biggest volcano in the Solar System: more than 40 km tall from base to summit.

detours.label: Fly along the dust trail of an old comet: about 1 hour later
detours.fact: Meteor showers happen when Earth passes through the trail of dust a comet leaves behind.

detours.label: Photograph the Milky Way with no air in the way: about 1 hour later
detours.fact: Our galaxy, the Milky Way, holds an estimated 100 to 400 billion stars.

detours.label: Take a long look back at Earth: about 2 hours later
detours.fact: Earth and Mars come closest about every 26 months, which is why Mars missions launch in windows that far apart.
